words-only.why: I checked each verifier check against its expect line. Check 1 passes on "exit code is 1 and `$d/out` is empty", which matches. Check 2 needs `bad config:`, the exact "$d/c.json", and line 3 and column 3 "in any readable form", so no exact wording is required. The proof's extra step, confirming the location doesn't come only from Node's message, is under Advisory. Check 3 passes when the script prints `OK` (it threw and the message has the path). Check 4 checks `listening on 9000`, exit 0 and `{"port":9000}`. Check 5 needs `npm test` to pass at the head and a path-checking test to fail with the base's src, matching the words. The stricter items (computed location, `cause`, ENOENT, no defaults returned) are all under "Advisory (does not affect PASS or FAIL)". Running on Node v22 is a setup step, not a condition.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs against the 6 tracked files and the scripts in package.json (`"test":"node --test"`). Both briefs name only files that exist: `src/app.js`, `src/config.js`, `test/config.test.js` and README. The builder's manual commands use valid `printf`/`mktemp` syntax, and the second line reuses `$d` set by the first. The verifier's Check 1 and Check 2 commands use valid redirection and quoting. The Check 3 and Check 4 `node --input-type=module -e "import {loadConfig} from './src/config.js'; ..."` snippets are valid ESM JavaScript, and the shell expands `'$d/...'` correctly inside the double quotes. Check 5 runs `npm test`, `git merge-base HEAD <target>`, `git checkout <base-sha> -- src` and `git checkout HEAD -- src`. These are valid git commands. The placeholders are clearly meant to be filled in, as in the issue's own proof (`<base>`). The `child_process.spawnSync` suggestion is a real Node API. No command needs a missing file or tool.

catches-traps.why:
I checked both must_catch items against the builder brief, and both are covered.

Item 1 (non-goal): the Goal paragraph says "Do NOT catch the error and return `{}` or defaults", and the brief says "`loadConfig` must still throw on malformed JSON". Its Out of scope list also includes "swallowing parse errors".

Item 2 (SyntaxError test): Current code says "That file already has a test asserting that bad JSON throws a `SyntaxError`." Step 1 tells the builder to throw a new error and adds "Throwing a `SyntaxError` keeps the existing test passing." That names the test in test/config.test.js and makes clear that wrapping in a different error type would change its outcome. Step 4 repeats "Keep the existing tests passing."

Both items are handled, so the criterion holds.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked both must_not items, and neither one shows up in the briefs. Item 1: the builder brief does wrap `JSON.parse` in a try/catch, but only to rethrow. It says to "throw a new error whose `message` includes the path", and it warns against returning a value: "Do NOT catch the error and return `{}` or defaults". So it never tells the builder to return a value on a parse error. Item 2: verifier Check 2 accepts line 3 and column 3 "in any readable form (for example `line 3 column 3` or `3:3`)". It fails a run only if a required item is missing or the line or column isn't 3. Its path check needs the exact path string, which the expect line requires, and it doesn't fix a format or an order. The builder's "Example format" is only an example and doesn't bind the verifier.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief with each verifier check. It has no PASS/FAIL wording. It does not copy Check 3's inline `node --input-type=module -e "...includes('$d/b.json') ? 'OK'..."` script, and it does not copy Check 5's method of checking out the base `src/`. The step 6 manual commands (`printf '{\n  "port": 9000,...' > $d/c.json; node src/app.js $d/c.json; echo $?` and the ok.json run) are trimmed versions of the issue's proofs 1 and 4. The criterion allows commands that the proofs name. The test inputs (`{port: 9000`, the four-line file, line 3 column 3) come straight from the issue's expect lines. The brief uses them only to tell the builder what its own tests should check, which is allowed. Step 2 tells the builder to compute line and column itself. That states the bar from the issue's proof 2. It is not the verifier's procedure for reading the code. So the builder gets the bar, not the checker's probes.
